name: Synthesize a whole drum kit (808, kick, clap, snare, closed and open hat) from a basic synth: sine and noise sources, envelope-drawn transients, fast pitch envelopes, and targeted EQ, then test and re-tweak each sound inside a real beat
goal: Build six drum sounds in one synth with no samples. 808: sine tuned so its fundamental sits around 45 Hz (an octave below where it first lands), plus a saw and white noise whose levels follow a drawn envelope with a quick dip for the transient; low-pass the saw; boost mids a little, soft-clip, use a very gentle high-pass around 20 Hz (a steep one sounds bad), and a narrow bell cut around 78 Hz; optional parallel copy with reverb faded in and kept to the sides. Kick: sine pitched down, very short amp envelope, a very fast pitch envelope (about 0.07 s) on pitch, soft clip, light bit-crush, multiband drive, cut boxy mids around 400 Hz, high-pass. Clap: white noise whose level envelope has three quick transients then one longer decay (about 0.085 s spacing on a 9-step grid), band-limited (energy above about 600 Hz, key areas about 1 kHz and 6 kHz), high end added with bells not shelves, a little chorus and very short delays for width, compression, reduce side highs. Snare: two or three sines in octaves (the reference showed tones at about 240, 484 and 1 kHz), noise with two quick transients, one shared filter, a very short pitch envelope on all tones, distortion; optionally layer the clap. Closed hat: white noise, about 0.22 s envelope, band/high-pass that keeps some mids. Open hat: longer noise envelope with a second transient, low-cut reverb, very short (1/64) ping-pong delay, shorten decay to taste. Render each and tweak inside a beat (e.g. re-export pitched up a few semitones).

source.title: The VITAL Drum Sound Design Tutorial!! (FREE PLUGIN)
source.transcript_note: Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

prerequisites: A synth with sine/saw oscillators, white noise, drawable envelopes or multi-stage LFOs in envelope mode, two filters and basic FX
A DAW to render and test the sounds in a beat

inputs.name: kit_targets
inputs.description: Which of 808, kick, clap, snare, closed hat, open hat to build

outputs.name: drum_samples
outputs.description: Rendered one-shots for each kit piece

outputs.name: drum_patches
outputs.description: Editable synth patches for each piece

outputs.name: test_beat
outputs.description: A short beat used to audition and refine the kit

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Third-party plug-ins named in the video (mastering suite, saturator, multiband distortion) are replaced by generic EQ, soft clip, multiband drive and limiter.
The 78 Hz narrow cut on the 808 is the speaker's ear-matched trick from a reference; tune the notch to taste for your 808 pitch.
Hats and claps are judged in context: a sound that seems fine solo can be too low or too bright in a loop.
For Polyrhythm Studio/Web Audio: oscillators + noise buffer + gain envelopes + biquad filters reproduce every recipe here.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: 808: sine osc tuned so the fundamental reads about 45 Hz on an analyser; add a saw and white noise whose levels follow a drawn envelope (quick dip at the start for a transient, then decay, about 1.6 s overall); low-pass the saw.
steps.expect: A deep sine 808 with a short gritty attack.

steps.action: 808 processing: small mid boost, soft distortion with modest drive, very gentle high-pass near 20 Hz (not steep), narrow bell cut around 78 Hz; optional parallel copy with reverb faded in, kept to the sides, then a limiter on the pair.
steps.expect: Full low end without boom smear; the steep-HP version sounds clearly worse.

steps.action: Kick: sine pitched down an octave, very short amp envelope, a very fast envelope (about 0.07 s) routed to pitch, soft clip; then light bit-crush, multiband drive, a cut around 400 Hz for boxiness and a high-pass.
steps.expect: A short punchy kick with a pitch-drop click.

steps.action: Clap: white noise with a level envelope of three quick transients then one longer decay (grid of about 9 steps, about 0.085 s); band-pass it so energy sits above about 600 Hz with emphasis near 1 kHz and 6 kHz; add highs with bells not shelves and avoid much content above about 11 kHz.
steps.expect: A recognisable clap 'flam' with no harsh fizz.

steps.action: Clap finishing: a little chorus and very short delays for stereo, compression, then turn down side highs.

Snare: two or three sines an octave apart (reference tones about 240 Hz, 484 Hz, 1 kHz), white noise with two quick transients, all through one filter; route a very short envelope to the pitch of every tone; add distortion; optionally layer the clap and blend.
steps.expect: A tonal snappy snare distinct from the clap.

steps.action: Closed hat: white noise with a very short envelope (about 0.22 s), filter to a tick, high-pass but keep some mids. Open hat: same noise, longer envelope with a second small transient, low-cut reverb and a 1/64 ping-pong delay, then shorten the decay.
steps.expect: Closed tick and open wash from one source.

steps.action: Render all pieces, build a short beat, and adjust each sound in context (EQ, decay, pitch shift a few semitones and re-export) until they sit together.
steps.expect: A coherent kit validated in a real groove.

verification: Analyser shows the 808 fundamental near 45 Hz and no steep high-pass slope.
The clap waveform shows three discrete bursts before the decay.
Snare shows octave-related tonal peaks plus noise; hats have little energy below a few kHz but are not purely top-end.
Every piece was auditioned and adjusted in a beat, not only solo.
